headline: High: Rasa can ingest and act on content while the paired content-writing agent has broad egress, creating default-path leakage and cascading misaction risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path because agent_b exposes chat channels and treats incoming text as dialogue, while agent_a is a content-writing source that can emit arbitrary text. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b chat channels without sanitization, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF agent_b treats user-visible text from agent_a as instructions, THEN attacker-controlled content can steer responses.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction hierarchy for imported text.
Strip or neutralize markdown, code fences, and imperative phrases before handoff.
Require human review before forwarding agent_a output into agent_b.
Use a separate channel for data vs. instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches text and voice and can send data through multiple messaging APIs, while agent_a has broad network egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage is plausible but not proven; default-path risk is still meaningful because both can move content off-box.
conditions: IF agent_a content includes sensitive text and is forwarded into agent_b, THEN that content can leave the local boundary via messaging APIs.
IF either agent is connected to a third-party backend, THEN copied conversation content may be retained externally.
mitigations: Do not forward sensitive content between agents.
Redact names, IDs, and secrets before handoff.
Disable unnecessary outbound connectors in agent_b.
Route both agents through a local-only test workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on all inter-agent messages.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no documented shared write surface, and agent_b explicitly does not support multiple instances, which reduces concurrent mutation risk. agent_a is not runnable and has no IO surfaces, so overlap is limited; the remaining conflict is mainly around outbound channels rather than shared writes.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external channel, THEN message ordering conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b is run in parallel instances despite its stated limitation, THEN state collisions may occur.
mitigations: Run only one agent_b instance.
Separate outbound destinations per agent.
Avoid shared mutable resources.
Use queueing for handoffs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a customer-support bot that can operationalize text, so if it consumes agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing replies. agent_a is a content-writing source, making this a plausible producer-consumer chain; no verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as source material for agent_b replies without verification, THEN incorrect facts can be propagated.
IF agent_b is connected to live customer channels, THEN cascaded errors become user-visible.
mitigations: Require fact-checking before reply generation.
Keep agent_a output as draft-only.
Add a human approval step for customer-facing messages.
Log source provenance for each response.
requires-engineering: implement citation/verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source docs-only entries. Because the pair lacks compliance-specific evidence, only a low residual risk remains from agent_b's external messaging integrations; agent_a is not cited for a specific compliance regime because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through agent_b's external messaging connectors, THEN compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention settings differ across connected channels, THEN deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in connected channels.
Review connector retention defaults.
Document data flows before deployment.
Disable unused integrations.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
